candidates.statement: Order service returns HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, which the gateway surfaces as 502 on POST /v1/checkout; the failure originates in the order service, not the gateway.
candidates.uncertainty: Traces show order 500s but not the internal cause (DB pool, Redis, payment latency); logs were excluded, so the specific order-side fault is unconfirmed.

report.explanation: Traces show every checkout 502 correlates with an order-service 500 on POST /v1/orders, and metrics show 16 502s on /v1/checkout with p95 ~325ms. The bounded cause is order-service HTTP 500 propagating to the gateway. The specific order-side mechanism is not established by current evidence, so alternatives remain open.
missing_evidence: Order service logs/errors explaining the 500 on POST /v1/orders
Order service dependency metrics (postgresql, payment, inventory) to distinguish pool exhaustion, redis timeout, or downstream latency
Excluded gateway logs (ev-f430679fd864ea83-r0-gateway_logs) to confirm error propagation
